detailed_rationale:
KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration designs, manufactures and supplies fin-and-tube-type heat exchangers and related thermal solutions for the HVAC and refrigeration industries -- a component supplier riding India's strong air-conditioning and cold-chain demand growth. Headline growth is genuinely strong: FY26 (year to Mar 2026) revenue was about Rs 600 crore, up 40% YoY, with net profit of about Rs 76 crore, up 43% YoY (EPS Rs 12.30) -- broadly matching the quant screen's revenue_growth_1y of 39.3%. A subsidiary secured a fresh Rs 50.87 crore heat-exchanger order in July 2026, supporting continued order-book momentum, and the company holds a CRISIL credit rating.

However, several concrete, sourced red flags sit underneath the growth headline and materially temper the picture. First, cash generation has diverged sharply from reported profit: free cash flow was negative Rs 312 crore in FY26 despite the reported profit growth, funded partly by borrowings that jumped from Rs 33 crore (Mar 2025) to Rs 187 crore (Mar 2026) -- a real quality-of-earnings gap between accrual profit and actual cash generation. Second, working capital is deteriorating in both directions: debtor days rose from 79 to 106 and inventory days stand at a high 242, both consistent with revenue being booked well ahead of cash collection and/or a build-up of unsold stock. Third, and most concretely, the promoter has recently and actively sold shares -- a reported sale of 10 lakh shares reduced promoter holding by 5.1 percentage points in a single recent quarter, to 65.69% -- which is a direct, recent insider-selling signal rather than a passive or regulatory dilution of the kind seen in some other names in this batch. Fourth, the company carries a GST dispute (a Rs 4.95 crore tax order issued in June 2026) -- modest in absolute size but a compliance item worth tracking. The company pays no dividend despite profitability, consistent with reinvestment but also consistent with a business consuming more cash than it generates. Against all of this, the stock trades at an extreme valuation -- PE of about 104x and roughly 13x book value -- that assumes flawless continuation of the growth rate with none of the cash-flow or working-capital concerns mattering. ROE (14.3% latest, versus the quant screen's 18.0%) and ROCE (16.1% latest, versus the quant screen's 18.4%) are respectable but not exceptional for a stock priced this richly, and do not on their own explain a 104x multiple.
recommendation_rationale: The quant screen carries this as Hold, and its own value_score (8.8, near the bottom of this entire batch) already signals the valuation is extreme. My own research adds a further, more specific concern the quant screen's revenue/ROE-based scoring cannot see: reported profit growth of 43% YoY is happening alongside negative Rs 312 crore free cash flow, rising debtor and inventory days, debt-funded working capital, and a concrete recent promoter share sale (5.1 percentage points in one quarter) -- a genuine profit-versus-cash-flow divergence plus an insider-selling signal, not just an expensive-but-clean growth story. I cannot force this to Sell against a quant Hold, but I believe there is a real, specific case that this combination (cash-flow quality plus recent promoter selling plus a 104x multiple) could reasonably be a Sell, which is exactly the kind of tension the escalation channel exists for -- so I am escalating while leaving the call at Hold per the rules.
summary: KRN Heat Exchanger makes thermal components for air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment, and has grown revenue and profit strongly over the past year, helped by rising AC demand and new order wins. But the reported profit growth has not been matched by cash generation -- free cash flow was sharply negative this past year, funded by a jump in borrowings, and both receivables and inventory have been building up faster than sales. The promoter also recently sold a meaningful block of shares. All of this sits underneath a very expensive valuation. We rate it a Hold, but are flagging the combination of cash-flow weakness, working-capital deterioration and recent promoter selling for portfolio-manager attention rather than treating this as a routine call.
positive_para: Strong reported top-line and bottom-line growth (revenue +40%, profit +43% YoY in FY26) riding India's structural air-conditioning and cold-chain demand growth, continued new order wins (a Rs 50.87 crore subsidiary order in July 2026), and a maintained CRISIL credit rating.
negative_para: Reported profit growth has not converted to cash -- free cash flow was negative Rs 312 crore in FY26, funded by borrowings that jumped from Rs 33 crore to Rs 187 crore -- while debtor days (79 to 106) and inventory days (242) both point to working capital building up faster than the business is collecting or selling through it. The promoter has also recently and concretely sold shares (10 lakh shares, cutting the stake by 5.1 percentage points in a single quarter), a direct insider-selling signal, and the stock is nonetheless priced at an extreme 104x trailing earnings and about 13x book value that assumes none of this matters.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At about 104x trailing earnings and 13x book value, the market is pricing several more years of 30-40%+ growth with no execution hiccups -- a very high bar that is directly in tension with this year's negative Rs 312 crore free cash flow, worsening receivable/inventory days, and a promoter who has just reduced their own stake. Even crediting genuine demand tailwinds in HVAC/cold-chain components, this valuation leaves essentially no room for the cash-flow and working-capital concerns to matter, which is precisely why they are escalated above rather than absorbed quietly into a routine Hold. Growth here is estimated below the 25% hypergrowth band specifically because the reported 40% pace is not yet confirmed by cash generation, so the ROE/dilution disclosure is not separately triggered -- though note that further growth funding, given already-negative FCF and rising debt, may well require additional capital (debt or equity) ahead.
escalation_reason: Reported FY26 profit growth (+43% YoY) is happening alongside negative Rs 312 crore free cash flow (funded by borrowings rising from Rs 33 crore to Rs 187 crore), worsening debtor days (79 to 106) and high inventory days (242), and a concrete recent promoter share sale (10 lakh shares, cutting the promoter stake by 5.1 percentage points in one quarter to 65.69%). This combination -- profit-vs-cash-flow divergence plus recent, specific insider selling -- sits underneath an extreme 104x PE / 13x book valuation. I believe there is a genuine, defensible case this could be a Sell on quality-of-earnings and governance grounds despite the strong reported growth; the quant framework's rock-bottom value_score (8.8) already flags the valuation extremity but cannot see the cash-flow/promoter-selling detail. Given the asymmetric-override rule I cannot convert this quant Hold to Sell myself, so flagging for portfolio-manager review.
